items.title: AI-based clinician decision support system for diagnosis of inherited retinal diseases: a multicenter, randomized trial.
items.body: The accurate and timely diagnosis of inherited retinal diseases (IRDs) represents an unmet clinical need in ophthalmology, as the current pathways rely on resource-intensive phenotyping, multidisciplinary expertise and genetic testing. Here we developed Retina4IRD, an artificial intelligence (AI)-based clinician decision support system (CDSS) that predicts 17 genotype categories from retina images. Retina4IRD uses a Vision Transformer model pretrained with RETFound. We then trained and validated Retina4IRD using multimodal data with color fundus photographs and optical coherence tomography scans from 1,843 genetically confirmed patients (3,376 eyes) across China, South Korea and Poland. The top-5 prediction accuracy was 0.904 (95% confidence interval (CI): 0.896-0.912) and 0.856 (95% CI: 0.850-0.863) for internal and external validation, respectively. We conducted a randomized controlled trial with 300 participants with suspected IRD randomized 1:1 to either Retina4IRD-assisted specialist arm or specialist-only arm. Of these, 295 participants (median age 33 years, 114 (38.6%) females) with available next-generation sequencing reports were included in the final analysis. The primary outcome was met: top-5 genetic accuracy was significantly higher in the Retina4IRD-assisted specialist arm versus the specialist-only arm (88.5% versus 67.3%, P < 0.001). For secondary endpoints, top-1 to top-4 accuracies all favored the Retina4IRD-assisted specialist arm, with top-1 accuracy of 37.8% versus 22.4% and top-4 accuracy of 81.8% versus 53.1%, respectively. Post hoc analyses demonstrated that, with Retina4IRD assistance, clinicians made better management decisions, and the composite downstream management score indicated significantly higher scores relative to the control group (37.7 versus 28.5, P < 0.001). Our study shows that Retina4IRD is a CDSS tool prior to genetic testing and aligns with clinical workflow for patients with suspected IRDs. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06839170 .
items.why: In a multicenter randomized controlled trial (RCT) of 295 patients with suspected inherited retinal disease (IRD), an AI-based clinician decision support system (CDSS) called Retina4IRD, built on a Vision Transformer pretrained with RETFound and validated across China, South Korea, and Poland, significantly improved genotype prediction accuracy when used to assist specialists compared to specialists alone (top-5 accuracy 88.5% vs 67.3%, P<0.001), and also improved downstream clinical management scores. This is a rare example of a prospectively validated AI tool with external validation across countries and a hard clinical endpoint (management decisions), making it a strong model for how AI-assisted genetic diagnosis could be integrated into real ophthalmology workflows.
items.plain: Scientists built an AI tool that looks at eye scans to help predict which of 17 genetic conditions is causing a patient's inherited eye disease, and tested it in a randomized trial with 295 patients across multiple countries. When doctors used the AI's suggestions, they correctly identified the right genetic cause far more often (89% of the time within their top 5 guesses, versus 67% without the AI) and made better treatment decisions afterward. This is a well-tested, real-world example of AI meaningfully improving diagnosis and patient care, not just a lab experiment.

glossary.definition: A group of genetic eye conditions that damage the light-sensing layer at the back of the eye, often leading to vision loss.
Software that gives doctors extra information or suggestions to help them make better medical decisions, without replacing their judgment.
A type of AI model designed to analyze images, often by breaking them into patches and learning patterns across the whole image.
Testing a model on data from a different location or population than it was built with, to see if it still works.
A study where participants are randomly assigned to different treatments or interventions, which helps ensure fair comparison and reduces bias.
A looser measure of correctness where the model's answer counts as right if the true answer appears anywhere among its five best guesses, rather than requiring the single top guess to be correct.

items.title: A deep learning model for speech-based prediction of clinical scores in people with Huntington's disease: a longitudinal study with cross-sectional replication.
items.body: BACKGROUND: Sensitive monitoring tools are needed to track progression in neurodegenerative diseases and assess interventions before overt brain damage occurs. We propose speech as a non-invasive, easily collected biomarker to capture disease-related variation over time. We developed and validated Neurodegenerative Disease Speech Network (NDSNet), an automated deep learning model that generates individual speech-derived estimates of contemporaneous clinical scores at each visit in people with Huntington's disease, from presymptomatic stages (Huntington's Disease Integrated Staging System [HD-ISS] stages 0-1) to symptomatic stages (HD-ISS stages 2-3). METHODS: We included data from people with Huntington's disease and healthy controls from three prospective longitudinal studies (Bio-HD, REPAIR-HD, and MIG-HD) with speech recordings and Unified Huntington's Disease Rating Scale (UHDRS) scores. NDSNet combines a pre-trained wav2vec 2.0 model and a recurrent attentive network in a contrastive learning framework for processing audio waveforms of speech. We trained and cross-validated (10-fold) NDSNet to predict the observed UHDRS scores in people with Huntington's disease across visits, with external validation in a replication cohort (the TPMH study). We then compared NDSNet predictions with striatal atrophy on MRI, the best-established marker of Huntington's disease progression. FINDINGS: Our developmental cohort included 191 people with Huntington's disease and 58 healthy controls, with speech data collected between 2001 and 2025 (MIG-HD data collected in 2001-13 and REPAIR-HD and Bio-HD data collected in 2018-25). The replication cohort included 110 people with Huntington's disease, of whom 78 were not included in the developmental cohort, with speech data collected between Oct 10, 2022, and Feb 5, 2024. In the developmental cohort, we analysed speech recordings obtained from 146 people with Huntington's disease (62 with brain MRI). Relative error between NDSNet predictions and observed clinical scores was 11·4% (95% CI 9·7-12·5) overall. The intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) between NDSNet-predicted and observed motor scores (ICC 0·87 [95% CI 0·83-0·91]) was similar to that for clinician ratings (ICC 0·847). Predictions showed strong temporal association and responsiveness to observed clinical change at the individual level. Performance remained consistent in 67 people with Huntington's disease in the replication cohort (after excluding 32 participants already included in the developmental cohort; relative error 15·0% [13·0-19·0]; ICC 0·67 [0·38-0·71]). Predicted scores showed MRI associations similar to those of observed clinical scores across symptomatic stages, and stronger associations with striatal atrophy at HD-ISS stages 0-1. INTERPRETATION: NDSNet predictions captured clinically relevant progression from speech in people with Huntington's disease, showed neuroanatomical grounding across disease symptomatic stages, and estimated the subclinical state at HD-ISS stages 0-1. These findings support the use of NDSNet as a scalable tool to complement standard assessments for longitudinal monitoring in Huntington's disease. FUNDING: Neuratris and Centre de Référence Maladies Rares-Maladie de Huntington.
items.why: A deep learning model (NDSNet) combining a pretrained wav2vec 2.0 speech encoder with a recurrent attentive network was trained on speech recordings from three prospective longitudinal cohorts of Huntington's disease patients and healthy controls, then externally validated in an independent replication cohort, predicting Unified Huntington's Disease Rating Scale (UHDRS) motor scores with an intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) of 0.87, comparable to inter-clinician reliability (ICC 0.847). This is a rare example of a speech biomarker for a neurodegenerative disease with genuine external validation and longitudinal tracking of individual change, suggesting real potential as a low-burden, remote progression marker, though it is Huntington-specific and its generalization to other neurodegenerative diseases is untested.
items.plain: Researchers built an AI system that listens to how people with Huntington's disease speak and estimates their clinical disability scores, testing it on recordings from several long-term studies and then checking it again on a completely separate group of patients. The AI's estimates matched actual doctor-assessed scores about as closely as two different doctors would agree with each other, suggesting speech could become an easy, non-invasive way to track this disease over time, though it's only been shown to work for Huntington's so far.

glossary.definition: A pretrained AI model that learns useful representations of raw audio, often reused as a building block in speech analysis systems.
A statistic that measures how closely two sets of measurements, such as two raters or a model and a rater, agree with each other.
A standard clinical scoring system used by doctors to measure the severity of symptoms in Huntington's disease.
Testing a model on data from a different location or population than it was built with, to see if it still works.
Research that follows the same participants forward in time, collecting data at multiple points, rather than looking backward at existing records.

items.title: Evaluating large language models for assessment of psychosis risk.
items.body: Psychosis prevention relies on early detection of individuals at clinical high risk for psychosis (CHR-P). The effectiveness of the CHR-P state is constrained, in part, due to clinical assessments requiring specialist interpretation of narrative interviews, limiting scalability. Here, we evaluate whether large language models (LLMs; deep learning models trained on large text corpora to process and generate language) can extract clinically meaningful information from such interviews to support psychosis risk assessment. We assessed 11 open-weight LLMs on 678 partial PSYCHS interview transcripts from 373 participants (77.7% CHR-P). Models inferred CHR-P status and estimated severity and frequency across 15 symptom domains, benchmarked against researcher-rated scores. Larger models achieved the strongest classification performance (Llama-3.3-70B: accuracy = 0.80, sensitivity = 0.93, specificity = 0.58). LLM-generated symptom scores showed good correlations with researcher-rated scores (ICC= 0.74, ICC= 0.75). Performance disparities were minimal across most demographic groups but varied across sites. Generated summaries were largely faithful to source transcripts, with low rates of clinically relevant confabulation (3%). Errors primarily reflected over-pathologisation of non-clinical experiences. While accuracy scaled with model size, smaller models achieved competitive performance with substantially lower computational cost. These findings demonstrate that open-weight LLMs have the potential to assess psychosis risk from psychometric interview transcripts, supporting scalable, human-in-the-loop approaches to early detection.
items.why: Researchers evaluated 11 open-weight large language models (LLMs) on 678 partial interview transcripts from 373 participants to assess clinical high risk for psychosis (CHR-P), finding the best model (Llama-3.3-70B) achieved 80% accuracy, 93% sensitivity, and 58% specificity against researcher-rated diagnoses, with symptom severity scores correlating well with human raters (intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) around 0.74-0.75). The multi-site design and attention to confabulation rates (3%) strengthen the evidence, though the low specificity and reliance on transcript-based assessment limit its readiness for standalone clinical use.
items.plain: Scientists tested 11 different AI language models to see if they could read transcripts of psychiatric interviews and correctly flag people at risk for psychosis, comparing the AI's judgments to those of trained clinicians. The best AI model correctly identified 93% of at-risk individuals but also had many false positives, correctly ruling out only 58% of people who were not at risk, and it rarely made up false information (only 3% of summaries). This suggests AI could help scale up early psychosis screening, but it still needs improvement before it can replace expert judgment.

glossary.definition: AI systems trained on huge amounts of text that can understand and generate human-like language.
A recognized early warning state in which a person shows mild or emerging symptoms that increase their chance of later developing a full psychotic disorder.
The percentage of true positive cases that a test or model correctly identifies.
The percentage of true negative cases that a test or model correctly identifies as negative.
A statistic that measures how closely two sets of measurements, such as two raters or a model and a rater, agree with each other.
When an AI model generates information that sounds plausible but is not actually supported by the source material.

items.title: An explainable machine learning approach for cervical cancer screening: decoding morphological diagnostic drivers.
items.body: BACKGROUND: Cervical cancer screening in primary care is hindered by expert pathologist shortages and heavy diagnostic workloads, leading to fatigue-induced misdiagnoses. This study evaluated the diagnostic capacity, subpopulation robustness, and operational efficiency of an interpretable machine learning (ML) tool within a large Chinese healthcare network. METHODS: A retrospective database of 5,000 women was audited. Archived liquid-based cytology (LBC) digital slides were evaluated via a parallel validation channel: the LBC-NET pipeline versus a double-blind panel of senior cytopathologists. Diagnostic safety was tested by stratifying data across age, vaginal infections, and menopause conditions. Algorithmic transparency was quantified using game-theoretic Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and morphological feature tracking. Operational efficiency was evaluated via continuous cumulative distribution curves. RESULTS: For detecting high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions or worse (HSIL+), the ML model achieved a clinical sensitivity of 92.5%, significantly outperforming the manual method at 84.2% ( < 0.001), with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.94. Subgroup stratification demonstrated that menopausal tissue atrophy or active vaginal infections caused no significant performance degradation ( > 0.05). SHAP analytics revealed that the nucleus-to-cytoplasmic ratio and nuclear hyperchromasia intensity were the core predictive metrics. Operationally, the ML system compressed the median slide-review time by 63.0%, escalating the daily screening capacity by 175% and reducing specialist referral consultations by 45.2%. CONCLUSION: The interpretable ML tool provides a reliable and fast clinical choice for massive cervical cancer screening.
items.why: In a retrospective cohort of 5,000 women, this interpretable machine learning (ML) pipeline for liquid-based cytology (LBC) detected high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions or worse (HSIL+) with 92.5% sensitivity versus 84.2% for a double-blind panel of senior cytopathologists, achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.94, and showed no performance drop across menopausal or infected subgroups while cutting review time by 63%. The head-to-head comparison against expert pathologists and use of Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) for interpretability strengthen the findings, though single-center retrospective design and lack of external validation temper how confidently this generalizes to other populations and lab workflows.
items.plain: Researchers built an AI system to read cervical cancer screening slides and tested it against a panel of senior expert pathologists on 5,000 patient samples, finding the AI caught more true cases of serious pre-cancer changes, 92.5% of the time compared to 84.2% for the human experts, while also working just as well in older or infected patients and cutting the time needed to review each slide by nearly two thirds. This is a strong single-site study with a fair head-to-head comparison to real doctors, but it still needs to be tested at other hospitals and with other patient populations before we know it works as well everywhere.

glossary.definition: A method of preparing cervical cell samples in liquid rather than smearing them directly on a slide, which produces clearer samples for microscopic review.

glossary.term: High-grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesions or Worse (HSIL+)
glossary.definition: A category of abnormal cervical cell changes that carry a meaningful risk of progressing to cancer if untreated.
A single number from 0.5 to 1 that summarizes how well a test distinguishes between two groups, with 1 meaning perfect separation and 0.5 meaning no better than chance.
The percentage of true positive cases that a test or model correctly identifies.
A mathematical technique that assigns credit to each input feature for how much it contributed to a machine learning model's specific prediction, used to make AI decisions more understandable.

items.title: Reply to the letter to the editor: "Machine learning model for predicting preeclampsia-related adverse outcomes".
items.body: We thank Liu et al. for their constructive comments on our article reporting the internal and external validation of a reduced-feature machine learning model for the prediction of preeclampsia-related adverse outcomes. The letter raises four points, which we address in turn. Regarding calibration and clinical utility, we generated calibration curves for the gradient-boosted tree model in both cohorts. Neither cohort shows a systematic, clinically concerning miscalibration pattern; deviations are concentrated at the extremes of the risk distribution, where observations are fewest. Brier scores were 0.010 (German cohort) and 0.068 (North American cohort), indicating good overall probabilistic accuracy. We agree that a formal clinical utility analysis, such as net benefit across threshold probabilities, represents an important next step. Regarding incremental value over the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio, we note that while the ratio offers strong short-term rule-out performance, its positive predictive value for ruling in preeclampsia related adverse outcomes remains limited. Our model, which incorporates the sFlt 1/PlGF ratio alongside ten additional routine clinical features, achieved AUCs of 92% and 87% in the German and North American cohorts, respectively. A formal head-to head comparison remains an important direction for future work. Regarding dataset heterogeneity, we acknowledge the structural differences between cohorts as a relevant limitation, while noting that discriminative performance remained statistically indistinguishable across cohorts despite significant differences in baseline characteristics. Regarding longer-term outcomes, we agree this is a valuable direction and intend to pursue it as follow-up data become available.
items.why: This is a reply to a letter to the editor addressing methodological critiques of a previously published gradient-boosted tree model that predicts preeclampsia-related adverse outcomes, reporting external validation area under the curve (AUC) of 92% in a German cohort and 87% in a North American cohort, alongside calibration data (Brier scores 0.010 and 0.068). The exchange usefully clarifies the model's incremental value over the soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 to placental growth factor ratio (sFlt-1/PlGF) and its stable discrimination despite cohort heterogeneity, which matters for anyone evaluating this tool's readiness for clinical use, though a formal head-to-head comparison and clinical utility analysis are still pending.
items.plain: This is a follow-up discussion where the authors of an earlier study respond to criticism of their AI model that predicts serious complications from preeclampsia, showing that the model performed consistently well when tested on patients from two different countries. This matters because it adds confidence that the tool could work reliably in different settings, although the authors still need to directly compare it against an existing blood test and show it actually helps in real clinical decisions.

glossary.definition: A machine learning method that combines many simple decision rules built one after another, each correcting errors from the previous ones, to make an overall prediction.
Testing a model on data from a different location or population than it was built with, to see if it still works.
A single number from 0 to 1 summarizing how well a model distinguishes people with and without a condition, where 1 is perfect and 0.5 is no better than guessing.
A number measuring how accurate a set of probability predictions were, where lower values mean better accuracy.
A ratio of two proteins measured in blood, soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 and placental growth factor, used clinically to help assess risk of preeclampsia.
How well a model's predicted probabilities match the real-world frequency of the outcome it is predicting.

items.title: Natural Cycles Receives Sixth FDA Clearance for AI-Powered Fertility Algorithm
items.body: Birth control and cycle-tracking app Natural Cycles received its sixth FDA clearance for an updated version of its AI-powered NC° Fertility Algorithm. The company previously secured FDA clearances for its birth control app, integrations with Oura Ring and Apple Watch, and over-the-counter availability. The next-generation algorithm combines statistical modeling with machine learning trained on tens of millions of real-world fertility data points… The post Natural Cycles Receives Sixth FDA Clearance for AI-Powered Fertility Algorithm first appeared on .
items.why: Natural Cycles received its sixth FDA clearance for an updated version of its AI-powered fertility algorithm, which combines statistical modeling with machine learning trained on tens of millions of real-world data points; this is a real regulatory milestone for a consumer-facing fertility algorithm but the announcement provides no new performance metrics or validation study details for this specific clearance. Regulatory clearance track record matters for reproductive health AI adoption, though the lack of accuracy or effectiveness data for this version limits how much can be concluded.
items.plain: The fertility tracking app Natural Cycles got approval from the US Food and Drug Administration for the sixth time, this time for an updated version of its algorithm that predicts fertile days using machine learning trained on huge amounts of real-world cycle data. This is a meaningful regulatory step for a widely used app, but the announcement does not share any new numbers on how well the updated version actually performs.

glossary.definition: The FDA is the US government agency that reviews and approves drugs, devices, and some software for safety and effectiveness before they can be sold.
A method where computer programs improve their predictions by learning patterns from large amounts of data rather than following fixed rules.

items.title: Multi-modal Stacking Machine Learning Model for Predicting Lymph Node Metastasis in Cervical Cancer.
items.body: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To develop and validate a multi-modal stacking machine learning model integrating intratumoral and peritumoral habitat radiomics from multiparametric Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with clinicopathological variables for noninvasive preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis (LNM) in early- stage cervical cancer (ECC). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study with prospective validation analyzed 623 ECC patients divided into training (n = 311), internal validation (n = 187), and external validation (n = 125) cohorts. Preoperative T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), and contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (CE-T1WI) were used to cluster tumor voxels into homogeneous habitats via K-means. Habitat radiomic features were extracted from intratumoral and a 3-mm peritumoral expansion. A stacking ensemble framework was built with five base classifiers (logistic regression, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), Elastic Net logistic regression, Depthwise Separable Convolutional Attention (DSCA), and support vector machine (SVM) as first-level learners and an XGBoost-based Meta-model as the second-level learner. Performance was assessed by area under the curve (AUC), calibration curves, decision curve analysis, net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). RESULTS: Among base learners, the SVM-based ITH_integrated_score model performed best, with AUCs of 0.882, 0.865, and 0.845 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts. The Meta-learner achieved AUCs of 0.915, 0.895, and 0.875, and DeLong test confirmed it significantly outperformed all base learners (all P < 0.05). The Meta- model demonstrated excellent calibration and the highest clinical net benefit. NRI and IDI analyses confirmed significant incremental value over each base learner. CONCLUSION: This multimodal stacking ensemble model improves preoperative LNM prediction compared with unimodal approaches and may help guide individualized surgical and surveillance strategies.
items.why: This retrospective study with prospective external validation (n=125) built a stacking ensemble model combining tumor and peritumoral radiomic habitats from multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with clinical variables to predict lymph node metastasis (LNM) in early-stage cervical cancer, achieving area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.915, 0.895, and 0.875 across training, internal, and external cohorts, outperforming single classifiers. The multi-cohort design and formal statistical comparison (DeLong test) add credibility, but the model remains imaging-based diagnostics rather than a practice-changing intervention and needs prospective clinical impact testing.
items.plain: Researchers built a computer model that combines MRI scan patterns with patient data to predict whether cervical cancer has spread to lymph nodes before surgery, testing it on separate groups of patients including one from a different hospital, and it worked better than simpler versions of itself, correctly telling apart cases about 87 to 92 percent of the time depending on the group. This is a solid technical improvement but still needs to be tested in real clinical use to see if it actually changes how doctors treat patients.

glossary.definition: The spread of cancer cells from the original tumor to nearby lymph nodes, which is important for deciding on treatment intensity.
An MRI scan that captures several different types of image contrast from the same body region to give a fuller picture of tissue characteristics.
A single number from 0.5 to 1 that summarizes how well a test distinguishes between two groups, with 1 meaning perfect separation and 0.5 meaning no better than chance.
Testing a model on data from a different location or population than it was built with, to see if it still works.
A statistical test used to check whether the difference in accuracy between two prediction models is likely real rather than due to chance.

items.title: Improving laboratory workforce efficiency using AI-assisted digital cytology within an HPV-based cervical screening programme: A model-based evaluation for the NHS Cervical Screening Programmes.
items.body: OBJECTIVES: We aimed to estimate the time required to review and report cervical cytology slides within a Human Papillomavirus (HPV)-primary cervical cancer screening programme, where cytology is used for triage following a positive HPV test, comparing Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted digital cytology (Genius) with manual microscopy. DESIGN: A decision-tree model of the flow of slides through the National Health Service (NHS) England cervical screening cytology laboratory workflow, parameterised using published evidence and expert input. SETTING: Cytology laboratories within the NHS Cervical Screening Programme in England and Scotland. RESULTS: Screening and reporting 479,125 cytology slides annually in England was estimated to require 31,842 staff hours with AI-assisted digital cytology versus 103,151 hours with manual microscopy. The mean time per slide review and reporting was 4.0 vs 12.9 minutes, respectively, corresponding to a potential 69% increase in overall productivity. CONCLUSIONS: AI-assisted digital cytology can support more resilient cervical screening programmes in the UK and other countries by reducing staff time required for slide review and reporting. These findings may inform policymakers considering strategies to mitigate workforce shortages.
items.why: This decision-tree modeling study estimated that AI-assisted digital cytology (Genius) would reduce cervical cytology slide review time from 12.9 to 4.0 minutes per slide in the UK National Health Service (NHS) screening program, translating to a modeled 69% productivity gain across roughly 479,000 slides annually. The analysis is a workforce simulation based on published parameters rather than a prospective trial, so real-world throughput and diagnostic accuracy gains remain to be confirmed, but the scale and policy relevance make it worth noting.
items.plain: Researchers used a computer simulation to estimate how much faster cervical cancer screening could go if labs used an AI tool to help review slides instead of doing it all by hand, and they calculated it could cut the time needed per slide from about 13 minutes to 4 minutes, saving a huge amount of staff time nationally. This is just a projection based on existing data, not a real-world test, so the actual time savings and accuracy still need to be proven in practice.

glossary.definition: A method that maps out possible steps and outcomes in a process, like a flowchart, to estimate time or cost under different scenarios.

items.title: Non-contrast MRI Radiomics Nomogram for Predicting Recurrence and Progression-Free Survival in Cervical Cancer following Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy.
items.body: BACKGROUND: Accurate prognostic stratification following concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) for cervical cancer remains challenging. Existing approaches often rely on contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), which limits applicability in patients with renal dysfunction and in resourcelimited settings. We aimed to develop and validate a non-contrast MRI-based prognosis prediction model combined with clinical predictors to estimate recurrence risk and progression-free survival (PFS). MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 145 cervical cancer patients from two centers were retrospectively analyzed. The model-building cohort (n=114) was used to extract radiomics features from pre-treatment MRI, and an extreme gradient boosting classifier was developed. Clinical predictors were identified through univariate Cox and multivariate logistic regression analyses. A nomogram integrating radiomics and clinical variables was then constructed. External validation was performed in an independent cohort (n=31). Model performance was assessed by discrimination, calibration, and its ability to stratify patients into low- and high-risk groups for predicting 5-year PFS. RESULTS: The proposed method categorized patients into well-defined risk groups. Survival results varied greatly among groups. Kaplan-Meier analysis indicated that patients with high risk had a worse 5-year PFS compared to those with low risk. This result was observed in both the construction cohort (P < 0.001) and the external validation cohort (P=0.012). The prognostic performance was comparable to that of contrast-enhanced MRI-based models. A significant point to note is that no gadolinium administration was necessary. DISCUSSION: This study develops a radiomics nomogram that relies on non-contrast MRI. The model offers strong and tailored prognostic information. Imaging features and clinical predictors combined, which improved predictive accuracy. The approach increases accessibility, particularly for patients contraindicated for contrast or in low-resource settings. CONCLUSION: We developed and validated a non-contrast MRI radiomics nomogram that accurately predicts recurrence and 5-year PFS following CCRT in cervical cancer. The model offers a clinically applicable, cost-effective tool for personalized risk stratification.
items.why: This two-center retrospective study built an extreme gradient boosting radiomics nomogram from non-contrast magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to predict recurrence and progression-free survival (PFS) in 145 cervical cancer patients after concurrent chemoradiotherapy, showing significant risk stratification in both the training cohort (n=114, P<0.001) and an external validation cohort (n=31, P=0.012). The use of external validation and a gadolinium-free approach for resource-limited settings strengthens its practical relevance, though the validation cohort is small.
items.plain: Researchers built an AI tool that reads regular MRI scans, without needing an injected contrast dye, to predict which cervical cancer patients are likely to have their cancer come back after treatment, and it worked in both the group used to build it and a separate test group from another hospital. This matters because it could help identify high-risk patients using cheaper, safer scans, though the outside test group was quite small.

glossary.definition: A magnetic resonance imaging scan performed without injecting a contrast dye, making it safer and more accessible for patients with kidney problems or limited resources.
A technique that extracts detailed numerical patterns from medical images beyond what the eye can easily see.
A machine learning method that builds a strong predictive model by combining many weaker prediction rules in sequence.
A visual scoring tool that combines multiple risk factors to estimate an individual patient's probability of an outcome.
Testing a model on data from a different location or population than it was built with, to see if it still works.
The length of time during and after treatment that a patient lives without their disease getting worse.

items.title: Performance of Large Language Model-Based Chatbots in Primary Health Care Teleconsultations: A Comparison Between Human and Artificial Intelligence-Generated Responses.
items.body: INTRODUCTION: Telehealth is a strategic component of primary health care and has advanced in Brazil through the National Telehealth Program. Its benefits can be enhanced by artificial intelligence (AI), which has emerged as a promising tool. This study aims to compare the performance of real human and AI-generated responses to queries submitted to the teleconsultation services of the Telehealth Center of the UFMG Faculty of Medicine (NUTEL FM-UFMG), a member of the Telehealth Brazil Program. METHODS: This is a comparative cross-sectional study of 180 real human and AI-generated responses, evaluated in a blinded manner according to quality criteria (medical adequacy, conciseness, coherence, and comprehensibility), risk potential, authorship identification accuracy, and inquiry resolution. Data from NUTEL FM-UFMG (January 2020 to May 2024) were utilized, covering cardiology, endocrinology, and obstetrics/gynecology (OB-GYN). Statistical analysis included the Shapiro-Wilk test, Kruskal-Wallis test, Nemenyi multiple comparison test, chi-square test, and Fisher's exact test. RESULTS: Across all specialties, a significant difference was observed in comprehensibility, with AI mean scores surpassing those of humans. For the remaining quality criteria, as well as for risk potential and inquiry resolution, no significant differences were found, despite AI scoring higher than humans. Within specific specialties, significant differences was observed in endocrinology (except conciseness) and cardiology (in conciseness); AI showed superior means. Across all specialties, as well as individually within endocrinology and OB-GYN, the accuracy of authorship identification (human vs. AI) was statistically significant. CONCLUSION: Despite existing limitations, AI demonstrates substantial potential as a support tool for teleconsultation services.
items.why: This blinded cross-sectional study compared 942 real patient histories from human general practitioners against large language model (LLM)-generated responses in Brazilian telehealth teleconsultations, finding AI outperformed humans on comprehensibility with no significant differences in most other quality measures, including in obstetrics/gynecology (OB-GYN) consultations. The blinded design and reasonably large sample strengthen the evidence, though it is an observational comparison rather than a controlled trial of patient outcomes.
items.plain: Researchers compared how well an AI chatbot versus real doctors answered patient questions in a Brazilian telehealth program, including in women's health, and found the AI was easier to understand while performing about as well on accuracy and safety. This suggests AI could help with routine medical question-answering, though the study only measured response quality, not actual patient health outcomes.

scored.title: AI-based clinician decision support system for diagnosis of inherited retinal diseases: a multicenter, randomized trial.
scored.why: In a multicenter randomized controlled trial (RCT) of 295 patients with suspected inherited retinal disease (IRD), an AI-based clinician decision support system (CDSS) called Retina4IRD, built on a Vision Transformer pretrained with RETFound and validated across China, South Korea, and Poland, significantly improved genotype prediction accuracy when used to assist specialists compared to specialists alone (top-5 accuracy 88.5% vs 67.3%, P<0.001), and also improved downstream clinical management scores. This is a rare example of a prospectively validated AI tool with external validation across countries and a hard clinical endpoint (management decisions), making it a strong model for how AI-assisted genetic diagnosis could be integrated into real ophthalmology workflows.

scored.title: A deep learning model for speech-based prediction of clinical scores in people with Huntington's disease: a longitudinal study with cross-sectional replication.
scored.why: A deep learning model (NDSNet) combining a pretrained wav2vec 2.0 speech encoder with a recurrent attentive network was trained on speech recordings from three prospective longitudinal cohorts of Huntington's disease patients and healthy controls, then externally validated in an independent replication cohort, predicting Unified Huntington's Disease Rating Scale (UHDRS) motor scores with an intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) of 0.87, comparable to inter-clinician reliability (ICC 0.847). This is a rare example of a speech biomarker for a neurodegenerative disease with genuine external validation and longitudinal tracking of individual change, suggesting real potential as a low-burden, remote progression marker, though it is Huntington-specific and its generalization to other neurodegenerative diseases is untested.

scored.title: Evaluating large language models for assessment of psychosis risk.
scored.why: Researchers evaluated 11 open-weight large language models (LLMs) on 678 partial interview transcripts from 373 participants to assess clinical high risk for psychosis (CHR-P), finding the best model (Llama-3.3-70B) achieved 80% accuracy, 93% sensitivity, and 58% specificity against researcher-rated diagnoses, with symptom severity scores correlating well with human raters (intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) around 0.74-0.75). The multi-site design and attention to confabulation rates (3%) strengthen the evidence, though the low specificity and reliance on transcript-based assessment limit its readiness for standalone clinical use.

scored.title: An explainable machine learning approach for cervical cancer screening: decoding morphological diagnostic drivers.
scored.why: In a retrospective cohort of 5,000 women, this interpretable machine learning (ML) pipeline for liquid-based cytology (LBC) detected high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions or worse (HSIL+) with 92.5% sensitivity versus 84.2% for a double-blind panel of senior cytopathologists, achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.94, and showed no performance drop across menopausal or infected subgroups while cutting review time by 63%. The head-to-head comparison against expert pathologists and use of Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) for interpretability strengthen the findings, though single-center retrospective design and lack of external validation temper how confidently this generalizes to other populations and lab workflows.

scored.title: Reply to the letter to the editor: "Machine learning model for predicting preeclampsia-related adverse outcomes".
scored.why: This is a reply to a letter to the editor addressing methodological critiques of a previously published gradient-boosted tree model that predicts preeclampsia-related adverse outcomes, reporting external validation area under the curve (AUC) of 92% in a German cohort and 87% in a North American cohort, alongside calibration data (Brier scores 0.010 and 0.068). The exchange usefully clarifies the model's incremental value over the soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 to placental growth factor ratio (sFlt-1/PlGF) and its stable discrimination despite cohort heterogeneity, which matters for anyone evaluating this tool's readiness for clinical use, though a formal head-to-head comparison and clinical utility analysis are still pending.

scored.title: Natural Cycles Receives Sixth FDA Clearance for AI-Powered Fertility Algorithm
scored.why: Natural Cycles received its sixth FDA clearance for an updated version of its AI-powered fertility algorithm, which combines statistical modeling with machine learning trained on tens of millions of real-world data points; this is a real regulatory milestone for a consumer-facing fertility algorithm but the announcement provides no new performance metrics or validation study details for this specific clearance. Regulatory clearance track record matters for reproductive health AI adoption, though the lack of accuracy or effectiveness data for this version limits how much can be concluded.

scored.title: Multi-modal Stacking Machine Learning Model for Predicting Lymph Node Metastasis in Cervical Cancer.
scored.why: This retrospective study with prospective external validation (n=125) built a stacking ensemble model combining tumor and peritumoral radiomic habitats from multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with clinical variables to predict lymph node metastasis (LNM) in early-stage cervical cancer, achieving area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.915, 0.895, and 0.875 across training, internal, and external cohorts, outperforming single classifiers. The multi-cohort design and formal statistical comparison (DeLong test) add credibility, but the model remains imaging-based diagnostics rather than a practice-changing intervention and needs prospective clinical impact testing.

scored.title: Improving laboratory workforce efficiency using AI-assisted digital cytology within an HPV-based cervical screening programme: A model-based evaluation for the NHS Cervical Screening Programmes.
scored.why: This decision-tree modeling study estimated that AI-assisted digital cytology (Genius) would reduce cervical cytology slide review time from 12.9 to 4.0 minutes per slide in the UK National Health Service (NHS) screening program, translating to a modeled 69% productivity gain across roughly 479,000 slides annually. The analysis is a workforce simulation based on published parameters rather than a prospective trial, so real-world throughput and diagnostic accuracy gains remain to be confirmed, but the scale and policy relevance make it worth noting.

scored.title: Non-contrast MRI Radiomics Nomogram for Predicting Recurrence and Progression-Free Survival in Cervical Cancer following Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy.
scored.why: This two-center retrospective study built an extreme gradient boosting radiomics nomogram from non-contrast magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to predict recurrence and progression-free survival (PFS) in 145 cervical cancer patients after concurrent chemoradiotherapy, showing significant risk stratification in both the training cohort (n=114, P<0.001) and an external validation cohort (n=31, P=0.012). The use of external validation and a gadolinium-free approach for resource-limited settings strengthens its practical relevance, though the validation cohort is small.

scored.title: Performance of Large Language Model-Based Chatbots in Primary Health Care Teleconsultations: A Comparison Between Human and Artificial Intelligence-Generated Responses.
scored.why: This blinded cross-sectional study compared 942 real patient histories from human general practitioners against large language model (LLM)-generated responses in Brazilian telehealth teleconsultations, finding AI outperformed humans on comprehensibility with no significant differences in most other quality measures, including in obstetrics/gynecology (OB-GYN) consultations. The blinded design and reasonably large sample strengthen the evidence, though it is an observational comparison rather than a controlled trial of patient outcomes.

scored.title: Performance of artificial intelligence in the collection of patient history in general practice.
scored.why: This cross-sectional study compared artificial intelligence (AI) and general practitioner performance in collecting patient medical histories across 942 consultations from 204 French general practitioners, finding AI performed at least as well as humans, particularly for older patients and in categories like allergies and family history. The sample size and blinded comparison design lend it reasonable credibility, though it addresses an administrative task rather than a diagnostic or treatment decision, limiting direct clinical impact.

scored.source: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging
scored.title: Preoperative PET/CT phenotype of gastric-type endocervical adenocarcinoma: integrated morphological, metabolic, serological, and explainable machine-learning analysis.
scored.why: This retrospective study of 144 cervical cancer patients used explainable machine learning with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) on positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) morphological, metabolic, and serological features to differentiate gastric-type endocervical adenocarcinoma (GAS) from squamous cell carcinoma and usual-type adenocarcinoma, incorporating decision curve analysis alongside standard discrimination metrics. The identification of a distinct low-metabolism, aggressive-dissemination phenotype is clinically informative for a rare, hard-to-diagnose cancer subtype, but the modest single-cohort sample size and retrospective design limit generalizability.

scored.title: Perceptions of simulated artificial intelligence in medical consultations: associations with stress, memory, and perceived credibility.
scored.why: A randomized simulation study with 163 healthy volunteers compared human versus AI-styled (chatbot or avatar) delivery of bad news using a Wizard of Oz design, where participants believed they interacted with an AI but a human controlled responses; human-delivered consultations produced higher stress and salivary cortisol, while AI-styled chatbot interactions had the lowest memory retrieval. The study is a controlled simulation rather than real clinical deployment, and the deceptive AI framing limits how directly the findings translate to real AI-patient interactions in practice.

scored.title: Characterization and Validation of EHR Computable Phenotypes for Long COVID Using Patient-Reported Symptoms: Insights from the Nationwide RECOVER Program.
scored.why: Researchers trained a machine learning algorithm on electronic health record (EHR) data from 1,501 RECOVER-Adult cohort participants to identify patients with highly symptomatic Long COVID, achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.80 in a held-out test set. The study lacks external validation at other institutions and relies on a single cohort, so its generalizability to broader clinical populations remains unproven despite the practical goal of aiding trial recruitment and screening.

scored.title: Large language models for interpretation of health checkup results.
scored.why: Four large language models (LLMs, AI systems trained on massive text datasets to generate and interpret language) were tested on interpreting structured health checkup data from a Korean national insurance database, with accuracy on classifying results rising from 0.69 in zero-shot prompting to 0.95 with Chain-of-Thought prompting (a technique where the model is asked to reason step by step before answering), and near-perfect accuracy on simple biochemical markers but weaker performance on more complex multi-threshold measures like blood pressure. This is a retrospective benchmarking exercise without clinical deployment, patient outcomes, or external validation beyond a single database, so its value is limited to prompt-engineering insight rather than evidence that LLMs can be trusted for real interpretive tasks.

scored.title: Predictive modeling with machine learning for low birth weight in the state of São Paulo: a retrospective population-based study.
scored.why: Using a large retrospective population-based cohort of 2.5 million live births in São Paulo state from a national registry, this study compared logistic regression and random forest models to predict low birth weight (LBW), with the balanced logistic regression model reaching an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) of 0.850. The study's scale is notable, but it lacks external validation beyond the source registry and offers standard risk-factor associations rather than a novel predictive capability, limiting its practical impact for this reader.

scored.title: AI-derived oocyte morphology and follicular fluid biomarkers in donors.
scored.why: This exploratory study in 49 young oocyte donors linked artificial intelligence (AI)-derived oocyte morphology scores to follicular fluid biomarkers, finding positive associations between AI scores and glucose, cholesterol, high-density lipoprotein (HDL), anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH), and HSPG2/Perlecan levels in a subset of 25 donors. The small sample size and lack of external validation limit generalizability, but the work is a novel attempt to biologically ground AI-based oocyte scoring, which is directly relevant to improving objectivity in assisted reproduction.

scored.title: Data-driven endocrine-metabolic phenotypes in young women with polycystic ovary syndrome and associations with cardiometabolic risk markers.
scored.why: This cross-sectional study of 1,032 young women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) used principal component analysis (PCA) and Gaussian mixture model clustering, an unsupervised statistical method, to identify a thyroid/autoimmune-enriched subgroup associated with modest lipid-related cardiometabolic differences. The findings are exploratory and lack external validation or longitudinal follow-up, but the large tertiary-center cohort and reproductive endocrinology relevance make it a plausible hypothesis-generating contribution.

scored.title: Kompass Diagnostics Scales Rapid Finger-Prick Hormone Testing
scored.why: Kompass licensed a finger-prick hormone testing platform from the University of Chicago for fertility panels, with results in about 10 minutes, but no clinical validation data, accuracy figures, or comparison to standard lab assays is given. This is a commercialization announcement with a reproductive health angle but no algorithmic or AI component and no evidence base to assess.

scored.title: The promise of deep urine proteomics for diagnosis of cancer, neurologic, and metabolic diseases.
scored.why: This case-control diagnostic accuracy study used deep urine proteomics (Olink Explore 3072 platform) and machine learning to build multiprotein panels distinguishing nine diseases, including ovarian, endometrial, and cervical cancers, from healthy controls, reporting area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values up to 0.98 in groups of only 22 patients each. The exploratory design, tiny per-disease sample sizes, single time point of collection, and lack of external validation mean these accuracy figures are best read as upper-bound estimates rather than clinically actionable findings.

scored.title: Elevated Circulating AIF1L as a Cell-Free RNA Biomarker of Preeclampsia Impairs Trophoblast Function via Mitochondrial Dysregulation.
scored.why: This study combined weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) of placental and plasma transcriptomes with machine learning to build a 10-gene cell-free RNA (cfRNA) nomogram for preeclampsia diagnosis, reporting an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.989, and used cell culture experiments to show that the gene AIF1L affects trophoblast invasion via mitochondrial pathways. The diagnostic AUC is implausibly high for a real-world biomarker and the validation appears to be internal rather than independent external cohorts, so this reads as promising but unproven mechanistic and biomarker discovery work.

scored.title: Evidence integration: The transformative role of artificial intelligence in maternal health.
scored.why: This umbrella review synthesized 34 existing reviews on artificial intelligence (AI) applications in maternal health, covering risk prediction for complications like preeclampsia and gestational diabetes, and concluded that a persistent translation gap exists due to inconsistent external validation, interpretability, workflow integration, and prospective impact evaluation. As a review of reviews rather than new evidence, it mainly restates known limitations in the field without presenting novel data or a definitive path forward.

scored.title: Identification and importance analysis of osteoporosis risk factors in perimenopausal women based on the Transformer-LSTM hybrid model and SMOTE.
scored.why: A single-center retrospective study used a Transformer-long short-term memory (LSTM) hybrid model with synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) to identify osteoporosis risk factors in perimenopausal women, reporting an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.923 and modest gains over single-architecture baselines. There is no external validation, and the clinical actionability is limited since the top finding (a bone turnover marker as most predictive) is not itself novel.

scored.title: Fusion Gene Detection Enhances Clinical Outcome Prediction of Hepatocellular Carcinoma Through Machine Learning Analyses.
scored.why: A retrospective study of 200 hepatocellular carcinoma samples trained machine learning models combining a 20-gene fusion panel with clinical parameters, achieving 72.4% accuracy for 3-year survival prediction versus 49-70% for individual clinical markers, evaluated on an internal training and testing cohort split rather than an independent external validation. The improvement over existing markers is notable but the small sample and lack of external validation limit generalizability, and this is outside the reproductive space entirely.

scored.title: Machine Learning Analysis of Maternal Mortality Determinants in Nigeria: An Exploratory Study.
scored.why: This ecological study applied XGBoost and Random Forest machine learning algorithms to 1960-2024 national-level Nigerian data to rank socioeconomic and health-system predictors of maternal mortality, finding female education and service-sector employment as protective factors. The analysis is exploratory, uses aggregated country-level rather than patient-level data, and offers no external validation, limiting its use beyond hypothesis generation for policy.

scored.title: Explainable AI in Male Infertility: A Clinical Roadmap for Shared Decision-Making.
scored.why: This is a perspective article proposing a roadmap for explainable artificial intelligence (AI) in male infertility care, discussing methods like SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), local interpretable model-agnostic explanations (LIME), and saliency maps without presenting new data or evaluation. It is useful for framing governance and validation priorities but offers no empirical findings that would change current practice.

scored.title: Systems-level genomic analyses reveal shared mechanisms underlying endometriosis and sleep disorders.
scored.why: This study combined National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) cross-sectional data, bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR), and machine-learning gene prioritization to link endometriosis with sleep disorders, finding an association (odds ratio 2.64) and modest genetic evidence for a causal direction from sleep disorders to endometriosis risk. The findings are explicitly hypothesis-generating pending prospective and experimental validation, and machine learning plays only a minor supporting role in gene prioritization rather than being the central method.

scored.title: AI-based techniques in sperm detection.
scored.why: This is a narrative review summarizing recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted sperm detection for azoospermia and cryptozoospermia, covering deep learning image analysis, augmented reality platforms, and AI-integrated microfluidic systems, without presenting original data or a systematic evaluation. It is a useful orientation piece for a fast-moving subfield but offers no new evidence that would change clinical practice.

scored.title: The iPatient Meets the iDoctor.
scored.why: No abstract or study content is available for this JAMA piece titled 'The iPatient Meets the iDoctor,' and the title suggests a commentary or perspective piece rather than original research. Without substantive data, this cannot be evaluated for clinical or methodological significance and should be treated as low priority this week.

scored.title: How Generative AI Should Transform Clinical Decision Support.
scored.why: This is an opinion or perspective piece in JAMA on how generative artificial intelligence (AI) should be integrated into clinical decision support, but no abstract or evidentiary content is available to assess. Without empirical data, design, or results, it cannot be evaluated on the criteria that matter here and should be treated as commentary rather than substantive evidence.

scored.title: Using artificial intelligence to analyze violence against women in São Paulo.
scored.why: This study applied time-series decomposition and predictive modeling to 80,148 notifications of violence against women in São Paulo, reporting associations such as a 2.47-fold increased risk of sexual violence among pregnant women and projecting continued upward trends over 24 months. The analytic methods are largely descriptive statistics and simple time-series forecasting rather than substantive machine learning or clinical AI, and there is no diagnostic or treatment application, so relevance to this reader's clinical AI focus is limited.

scored.title: Mechanistic advances in nanomedicine, nucleic acid therapies, and AI-driven research on cervical cancer.
scored.why: This is a narrative review covering nanomedicine, nucleic acid therapeutics, and AI-assisted formulation optimization for cervical cancer drug delivery, with no original data or evaluation presented. It offers a broad conceptual overview rather than a testable finding, so it has limited value for a reader tracking evidence-based clinical AI progress.

scored.title: A prognostic immune signaling-related lncRNA-circRNA-mRNA network model for cervical cancer using machine learning.
scored.why: This retrospective bioinformatics study built a LASSO (least absolute shrinkage and selection operator) machine learning model from a long coding RNA (lncRNA)-circular RNA (circRNA)-messenger RNA (mRNA) network to prognosticate cervical cancer, reporting an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.77 in training and 0.89 in testing with only internal bootstrap validation. The lack of external validation and reliance on a small, discovery-focused molecular network limits clinical applicability at this stage.

scored.title: Deep Learning for Automated Classification and Dynamic Risk Prediction of Retained Products of Conception on Postpartum Ultrasound.
scored.why: This item concerns deep learning for automated classification and dynamic risk prediction of retained products of conception on postpartum ultrasound, but no abstract text is available to assess study design, sample size, or validation. Given the absence of substantive detail, it cannot be judged on the evaluation criteria this digest applies and is scored conservatively.

scored.title: An integrated deep learning and Bayesian computational method-based quantification of angiogenesis in the chick embryo model.
scored.why: This preclinical study developed a deep learning and Bayesian hierarchical Gompertz Gaussian process pipeline to quantify angiogenesis in the chick embryo yolk sac membrane model, validated pharmacologically against known pro- and anti-angiogenic agents. It is a laboratory image-analysis tool rather than a clinical or reproductive-medicine application, so its relevance to this digest's focus is limited despite methodological sophistication.

scored.source: Zhonghua Fu Chan Ke Za Zhi
scored.title: [Radiomics and deep learning in the prediction of spontaneous preterm birth using cervical ultrasound].
scored.why: This item on radiomics and deep learning for predicting spontaneous preterm birth from cervical ultrasound provides no abstract text, preventing assessment of study design, sample size, or validation approach. Given the complete lack of substantive detail, it must be scored conservatively despite the topic's relevance to obstetric risk prediction.

scored.title: PMOS Linked To Increased Cardiovascular Disease Risk, Study Finds
scored.why: This news item reports a large observational study of over 413,000 women linking polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS, a variant terminology likely referring to a polycystic ovary syndrome-related phenotype) with increased atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk independent of usual risk factors. The finding is clinically relevant to reproductive endocrinology, but it involves no algorithmic or AI component at all, placing it outside this digest's scope regardless of its epidemiological strength.

scored.title: Bonafide Survey Highlights Perimenopause Mental Health Toll
scored.why: This is a self-reported survey of 2,000 symptomatic women on perimenopause mental health symptoms, with no comparison group, validated instrument details, or algorithmic component described. It is market research from a company selling menopause products, not a clinical study, and has no AI relevance.

scored.title: TD Bank Group Donates $1M to Advance Menopause Brain Health Research
scored.why: A bank donated $1 million to fund an ongoing study of menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) for migraines and cognitive symptoms; this is a funding announcement, not a report of trial results, and has no AI component.
